stories.title: Of eight use of helmet infractions in Week 7, only Cam Skattebo was flagged
stories.summary: The fine imposed on Giants running back Cam Skattebo for illegal use of the helmet was not a rarity.
stories.detail: The fine imposed on Giants running back Cam Skattebo for illegal use of the helmet was not a rarity. The flag thrown in real time for it was. Of eight fines levied by the NFL for use-of-helmet violations in Week 7, only Skattebo's came with a flag. The league fined Skattebo $7,073. The seven players fined but not flagged were: Bears cornerback Clark Phillips ($11,550); Broncos safety Brandon Jones ($23,882); Broncos Alex Singleton ($47,662); Lions safety Brian Branch ($23,882); Colts cornerback Cam Taylor-Britt ($7,791); Steelers receiver Brandon Smith ($4,916); and 49ers running back Jordan James ($6,194). The fines increase as the violations repeat. For Singleton, who was fined $23,882 for illegal use of the helmet, it was the second straight week he was fined. The officials, for whatever reason, don't often call penalties for illegal use of the helmet. That's what made the penalty called on Skattebo so unusual. The fact that the hit flattened Texans safety M.J. Stewart likely was a factor in the decision to penalize Skattebo. Still, the fact that only one of eight instances resulted in a foul being called underscores the fact that, when it comes to the rule against lowering the…

stories.title: Position grades from Michigan Football’s narrow win at Rutgers
stories.summary: It once again wasn’t pretty, but Michigan Football got back in the win column by defeating Rutgers, 28-21. Here are our position grades from the game:
stories.detail: PISCATAWAY, NEW JERSEY - OCTOBER 31: Salesi Moa #12 of the Michigan Wolverines celebrates a catch against the Rutgers Scarlet Knights during the first half at SHI Stadium on October 31, 2026 in Piscataway, New Jersey. (Photo by Ed Mulholland/Getty Images) | Getty Images True to form, Michigan made things interesting, but still got the win 28-21 over Rutgers on Saturday. It definitely wasn’t perfect, but here’s a look at how each position group graded out in the victory. Quarterback – A- After a less-than-stellar debut as the starting quarterback last week, Tommy Carr looked really good against Rutgers. Granted, it was against a defense that isn’t scaring anyone (even on Halloween), but Carr went 22-of-27 for 266 yards and one touchdown. He also added 54 yards on the ground (82 excluding sacks) with two scores. The ground game was where Carr made his biggest impact, with his fourth-quarter touchdown deciding the game. He also extended several plays that he wasn’t well-protected and ended up being able to make something out of nothing through the air. He’ll get to make his first start in a rivalry game next week against Michigan State. ANOTHER TOMMY CARR RUSHING TOUCHDOWN! @UMichFoo…

stories.detail: Another brutal injury blow to the Los Angeles Chargers . Derwin James is headed to injured reserve, the team announced Saturday, Oct. 31. The Chargers will also be without guard Kayode Awosika (fibula), defensive back Deane Leonard (concussion) and receiver Brenen Thompson (quad/hamstring) for Sunday's Week 8 matchup against the Los Angeles Rams . James' setback is the latest in a litany of injuries to key players that have come to mire the winless Chargers' season. Tight end David Njoku injured his right knee/fibula in Week 2. stories.title: Ravens defense has provided tough test for Josh Allen
stories.summary: Examining how Allen has played against the Ravens defense
stories.detail: Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen has started against the Ravens six times — including the playoffs — in his NFL career before Week 8’s clash, and he hasn’t exactly flourished in those matchups with Baltimore. He’s been surprisingly held in check as a runner too. Allen’s average completion percentage in those six games is just 59.3%. His passing-yard average is just 211 with a pedestrian 6.06 yards-per-attempt average, and his rating is a mere 82.7. However, his touchdown-to-interception ratio is 5 to 1. His highest rushing-yard total (70) came in a 23-20 comeback in 2022. Other than that, Baltimore has held Allen to 30 yards or less on the ground. Allen has played the Ravens defense three times the past two years (twice in 2024), and of course, Baltimore’s personnel has changed over that time to a certain degree, but key pieces like Roquan Smith, Kyle Hamilton, and Marlon Humphrey remain. Despite his relative struggles against the Ravens in his NFL career to date… we can’t forget about Allen’s most recent outing facing this Baltimore team. teamStories.summary: The Jets announced a few roster moves ahead of their Week 8 matchup with the Raiders, including placing DT T'Vondre Sweat on injured reserve, putting him on the shelf for at least four weeks.
teamStories.detail: The Jets will be without DT T'Vondre Sweat for longer than initially thought. Gang Green is placing Sweat on injured reserve after suffering a knee injury in their Week 7 loss to the Dolphins. The team already ruled out Sweat for their Week 8 matchup with the Raiders this Sunday, but they will give the veteran lineman more time to heal up for the final stretch of the regular season. The Jets have a bye in Week 9 before they head into the second half of their schedule. The Jets are hopeful Sweat can return to the team before the end of the regular season. Sweat has played in all seven games this season and has registered 17 tackles and two tackles for loss. New York signed DT Payton Page to the active roster to take Sweat's place. They are also elevating OL Brand Banks and Edge Quinton Bell from the practice squad. Bell's elevation could mean rookie pass rusher David Bailey (groin) will miss Sunday's game. He was listed as doubtful after not practicing all week.

teamStories.summary: Geno Smith has been sacked 21 times and it’d be wise for Rob Leonard’s Las Vegas defense to aggressively attack New York
teamStories.detail: (Heidi Fang/Las Vegas Review-Journal/Tribune News Service via Getty Images) Geno Smith gets rattled when blitzed. That’s not some grand revelation on the veteran quarterback. It’s the plain truth and Raider Nation is all too aware of this. Smith was the Las Vegas Raiders starting quarterback last season for then-head coach Pete Carroll and the West Virginia product was like a lamb to slaughter that year. Due to a porous offensive line — due in large part to both talent and coaching — Smith was sacked a league-high 55 times while throwing 19 touchdowns and an NFL-leading 17 interceptions as a 15-game starter. Smith is enjoying a rebound season in his return to the New York Jets — the team that drafted him 39th overall in the 2013 NFL Draft — as he’s completing 70 percent of his passes with 10 touchdowns, two interceptions, and 1,623 passing yards. Smith is keeping Gang Green in games and still continues to throw a nice deep ball. But when opponents dial up the pressure and send extra defenders beyond the standard four-man rushes, Smith continues to wilt. Behind New York’s offensive line, Smith has been sacked 21 times which is fourth-most behind the Cleveland Browns’ Deshaun Watson…

stories.title: Reed Sheppard gets paid… well, kind of
stories.summary: Big news for Reed
stories.detail: Yesterday afternoon, Adam Spolane reported that the Houston Rockets had picked up Reed Sheppard’s fourth-year option. This means for the 2027-2028 season, Sheppard will be making just above $14 million before he is eligible for a rookie contract extension. It could be seen as an odd move for the Rockets, who had some questions about where Sheppard would fit into the rotation throughout this season, but it does seem like they want to keep him around for at least this year and next year before potentially extending him in free agency after the 2027 season. Sheppard is the 10th first-round pick the Rockets have selected from 2021-24. He is the sixth of 10 players to have his fourth-year option picked up by the team. The previous five, Jalen Green, Alperen Sengun, Jabari Smith Jr., Tari Eason and Amen Thompson, all inked contract extensions with Houston. After a rough debut year, Sheppard has become a fixture in the Rockets’ rotation. He moved into being Fred VanVleet’s backup at point guard from sliding completely out of the rotation. stories.detail: In a court filing this week, Jeanie Buss accused her siblings of conspiring against her in a "cloak and dagger" campaign through the media, said they were jealous that their father picked her over them to govern the Los Angeles Lakers and asked a judge to block her siblings' attempt to sell the family's shares in the team, which would end her run as the Lakers' governor. Wednesday's filing, reviewed by ESPN, is the latest salvo in the bitter legal battle playing out between Jeanie and her siblings, namely Joey and Jesse Buss, leading up to a scheduled Dec. 8 hearing in Los Angeles Superior Court. The filing responds to recent filings by Jeanie's siblings, who are seeking to sell the family's remaining shares of the Lakers to the Bob Iger and Josh Kushner ownership group, which is seeking to buy the team from Mark Walter at a $12.5 billion valuation. "The conflicts that ensued after Dr. [Jerry] Buss's death [in 2013] were sadly inevitable, and no doubt intensified given that Dr. Buss chose his daughter over four sons to be his successor," Jeanie's lawyers wrote in the Wednesday filing.
